claim: An advance record with three empty predecessor objects and five empty query strings meets the evidence contract.
reason: Length is not field/type/content validation. Required move, falsifier and predecessor evidence are absent.
scope: Mechanical record validity only; a structurally valid record need not be true.

claim: An orphan A-S1-P01-B01 survive record may generate S2 expansions.
reason: No eligible assigned parent claim or independent review provenance exists. The same applies if a parent exists but its claim/version changed.
scope: Stage identity and provenance, not substantive argument quality.

claim: Equal passive record distributions entail equal distributions under do(X=0).
expected: reject universal claim by explicit counterexample; do not classify this as an ontology dispute
witness: Z is a fair bit. Model A: X=Z, Y=X. Model B: X=Z, Y=Z. Both passively give (X,Y)=(0,0),(1,1), each with probability 1/2. Under replacement intervention do(X=0), A has Y=0 surely; B has Y=Z, with P(Y=1)=1/2.
reason: Passive observational equivalence does not establish equivalence under a larger intervention class.
scope: Two specified finite structural causal models and one replacement intervention; no new result or temporal-ontology discriminator claimed.

claim: One finite growing/completed-history model with equal records proves every growing/completed-history model has equal records.
expected: do not advance as a universal result; narrow claim or supply a proof
witness: The premise establishes an existential instance. It provides no quantifier-preserving argument for all dynamics, access protocols or model sizes.
reason: A finite example can illustrate agreement. It cannot prove an unrestricted universal claim. Conversely one admissible finite counterexample can refute a universal claim whose domain includes it.
scope: Logical scope check; no claim that the unrestricted physical equivalence is false.

claim: Define objective passage to mean increasing coarse-grained entropy; entropy increases in this model; therefore objective passage exists in the disputed metaphysical sense.
expected: reject the metaphysical inference; definition-relative conclusion alone is trivial
witness: The definition fixes a new predicate but provides no premise identifying it with the independent metaphysical target.
reason: The thermodynamic arrow and passage cannot be identified by stipulation as an independent discovery.
scope: Ambiguity/circularity calibration; does not deny entropy arrows or any particular defended passage theory.

claim: If only symmetry-invariant structure is ontologically privileged, and a specified model admits no unique invariant global simultaneity, then global simultaneity is not privileged under that criterion.
expected: do not kill solely because a philosophical bridge is explicit; assess validity, motivation, scope and prior work separately
witness: The inference is conditional on the declared criterion. It is not presented as physics alone refuting every presentist model.
reason: An explicit bridge argument is admissible philosophical work. This simple conditional may still be trivial or already known; the control does not instruct advancement.
scope: False-kill calibration, not a novel philosophical argument or proof that the bridge is justified.

claim: Presentism, truthmaker maximalism and absence of abstract truthmakers alone entail that a true past-directed proposition has no truthmaker.
expected: reject entailment as underspecified; require an additional premise excluding present concrete truthmakers
witness: A minimal interpretation contains one present concrete record r and one true past-directed proposition p, with truthmaker relation T(r,p). All existing objects in the domain are present and concrete; p has a truthmaker. No stated premise excludes T. Whether this relation is philosophically adequate is an additional disputed premise.
reason: An agent-generated gold label can smuggle the conclusion into an unstated truthmaker restriction. Mere stipulation of T is a logical counterinterpretation, not a defense of a substantive truthmaker theory.
scope: Logical non-entailment under the explicitly weak premises; not a solution to presentism's truthmaker problem.

claim: A completed-path representation by itself entails deterministic evolution.
expected: reject the representational inference under the specified dynamical notion of determinism
witness: Omega={(0,0),(0,1)} with each path assigned probability 1/2; coordinate X0=0 and X1 equal to the second component. The same initial coordinate has two dynamically allowed continuations with a nondegenerate transition distribution, even though each sample path is represented as a complete pair.
reason: Representing complete paths does not change uniqueness of continuation from a specified state. Hidden-state completions require additional state/dynamical assumptions.
scope: Finite stochastic process; neither future truth settledness nor metaphysical openness follows. Completed mathematical paths are not assumed to be ontologically actual.
